source.title: A Probabilistic Perspective on Unlearning and Alignment for Large Language Models
source.authors: Yan Scholten; Stephan Günnemann; Leo Schwinn

page_placements.theme: Recovery by sampling or alternative decoding

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses probabilistic sampling and leakage metrics to test whether unlearning evaluations that look successful under greedy decoding still leave recoverable targeted information. This is a different evaluation method from the listed recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper tests probabilistic sampling, not fine-tuning recovery, activation ablation, quantization, or prompt-only attacks. It cites logit-lens and embedding-space attacks but does not report results from those cited studies. Figure-only details for individual TOFU questions and entropy sweeps are not transcribed as numeric results. Alignment toxicity experiments are outside the targeted-knowledge claim.
record.test_reason: The study probes A's 'simple attacks don't recover it' with a new attack: multinomial (top-p) sampling instead of greedy decoding. It applies the attack to WHP Llama-2 and to TOFU models unlearned with GA, GD, RMU and NPO. It uses no fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization or prompt changes, so B–E are untested. Its own entropy method resists only sampling, not the listed attacks, so it is not an F test.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, but the paraphrase understates the authors' claims. They claim that simple multinomial sampling 'breaks all state-of-the-art unlearning algorithms' and retrieves most if not all unlearned information. They also claim greedy evaluations falsely indicate success. They propose entropy optimization with adaptive temperature, which they say reduces sampled leakage without hurting diversity or utility. The aggregate TOFU table supports a weaker version: sampled mean leakage equals greedy, and only the spread is larger.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates unlearning using top-p probabilistic sampling and distributional leakage metrics; it does not implement the claim's fine-tuning, activation-ablation, quantization, or prompt-only recovery attacks. It also proposes NPO plus entropy optimization and adaptive temperature scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Evaluation outcome differs between greedy decoding and probabilistic sampling; reported leakage also varies by unlearning method. The paper describes entropy regularization strength and temperature as affecting leakage and output diversity.

fits_no_version.finding: NPO combined with entropy minimization on the forget set and adaptive temperature thresholding brings TOFU sampled ROUGE-L SD to 0.00 and ED to 0.20, equal to greedy. Utility stays around 0.47–0.51.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A counter-method resists sampling-based extraction of unlearned knowledge. Sampling is not among the attacks listed in F.

record.problems: No never-trained comparison is reported for the sampled leakage results, so the study cannot establish recovery relative to a model that never learned the knowledge. TOFU plots include an individual question, while the tabulated aggregate is for the TOFU 90/10 split. The proposed entropy method is not tested against the specific attacks in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 3's individual-question distributions and bounds, and Figure 4's entropy/temperature sweep, are not transcribed because the supplied figure text does not provide assignable numeric values for each method or setting. Table 2 utility results are included as R22–R40.

untested.parts: Near-chance targeted accuracy against a never-trained or chance reference, and retention of general ability for the baseline methods. Attacks other than sampling.
All of it: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
All of it: no activation ablation or internal analysis.
All of it: prompts are fixed, with no rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages or in-context information.
The entropy method is not evaluated against the B–E attacks.

missing.what: Per-question TOFU ROUGE-L distributions under sampling versus the greedy value (GA vs preference optimization; NPO vs Ours), and the NPO general leakage bound Mgen
The exact greedy-decoding leakage value for WHP on Harry Potter Q&A, described as indicating no information

record.verdict_notes: WHP is an original-source model, but this study is not one of the original sources, so verdicts are allowed. The alignment (JailbreakBench toxicity) results fall outside the claim and are not recorded. Figure 4's temperature and λf sweeps concern the study's own method.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the listed fine-tuning, internal-edit, quantization, or prompt-only attacks. It does not compare recovered information with a model that never saw the knowledge, nor directly establish near-chance targeted accuracy.
Fine-tuning recovery with unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
Activation-direction ablation or evidence from internal edits that access is blocked rather than knowledge deleted.
Recovery by prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
The proposed entropy-optimization approach is evaluated against sampling, but not against the attacks listed in the claim or versions B–E.

rows.subject: Llama-2-Who-is-Harry-Potter model
rows.operation_detail: Compared greedy decoding with probabilistic sampling; answers checked for relevant keywords
rows.measure: Fraction of questions for which the upper bound on expected leakage exceeds 10%
rows.baseline: Greedy decoding indicated no information in the model
rows.note: The authors say sampling reveals correct responses and that deterministic evaluation underestimates residual leakage.
rows.check: V1 is invalid. The 38% is the share of questions whose Clopper-Pearson upper bound on leak probability exceeds 10%. It is not an observed leak rate, and the greedy baseline shows no leakage. This is the clearest recovery result, but it is still a bound.

relationships.condition: Llama-2 WHP model on Harry Potter Q&A, keyword leakage, top-p sampling with 1024 samples
relationships.reason: Greedy decoding shows no leakage, but under sampling 38% of questions have a leak-probability upper bound above 10%. The authors say the model 'still leaks information' (R21). The figure is a bound, not an observed rate.
relationships.display_finding: Greedy decoding showed no leakage, but sampling yielded leak-probability upper bounds above 10% for 38% of questions; these bounds do not establish observed leakage rates.

source_check.condition: Llama-2 WHP model on Harry Potter Q&A, keyword leakage, top-p sampling with 1024 samples
source_check.reason: The authors say greedy 'wrongly' shows no information while sampling makes the WHP model still give correct answers (R21). For 38% of questions the bound is above 10%. A's claim that simple attacks don't recover the knowledge fails where A says it holds. The reason already flags that the figure is a bound.

relationships.condition: Phi-1.5 on TOFU 90/10 unlearned with GA, GD, RMU or NPO, ROUGE-L under top-p sampling
relationships.reason: Sampled mean ROUGE-L matches or falls below greedy (R3, R7, R11, R15). Only modest spread (SD 0.05–0.10) shows occasional extra leakage (R4, R8, R12, R16), and the ED gains (R2, R6, R10, R14) come from that spread. There is no never-trained reference.
relationships.display_finding: Mean sampled ROUGE-L matched or fell below greedy decoding, but standard deviations of 0.05–0.10 reflected occasional extra leakage and drove ED gains.

relation.reason: Its sampling results bear on whether A holds.

tranche.reason: Sampling-based evaluation is a different method on the same question. T5 would also be defensible, since the authors argue that greedy evaluation misleads.

source_check.notes: Phi-1.5 is used for all TOFU runs. HP Q&A uses the WHP Llama-2 model, keyword match, top-p p=0.9, n=1024 and alpha=0.01. No never-trained reference exists, so A's near-chance part is untested. Table 2 prints two utilities for what looks like the same setting (lambda_f=1, lambda_r=0, 99/1): 0.496 in the left block and 0.492 in the right block, both as printed. RMU on TOFU barely unlearns even under greedy (det 0.70).

statements.correction: Conditions: sampling budgets up to 1024 (this study: n=1024 per question, top-p p=0.9, alpha=0.01). For the 'greedy hides leakage' point, cite only R21 from this study.
statements.problem: The part about this study is right: WHP model, no leakage under greedy, top-p sampling with 1024 samples, 38% of questions with a bound above 10%, and the bound caveat. Minor issues: the group conditions say 'sampling budgets up to 1000', but this study used 1024. Cited R3 (TOFU GA, sampled mean 0.31 vs greedy 0.32) shows no leakage hidden by greedy on average.

The part about this study (WHP, Harry Potter Q&A, greedy shows no leakage, top-p with 1024 samples, 38% of questions with a bound above 10%) matches Figure 3(a), Sec. 6.1 and Appendix A.1. The other numbers belong to other studies.

statements.correction: Phi-1.5, TOFU 90/10: Ours det 0.20, ED 0.20, mean 0.20, SD 0.00. Table 2 utility is 0.469-0.512 across the 90/95/99 splits and lambda_f/lambda_r settings.
statements.problem: The numbers match Table 1 (Ours, 90/10: det 0.20, ED 0.20, mean 0.20, SD 0.00) and Table 2 (utility 0.469-0.512). The utility range spans all Table 2 splits and lambda settings, including lambda_f=0 (plain NPO). Table 1's Ours run has no separate utility figure. SD 0.00 is partly by design: tau is set to 0 when confidence is above 0.9.
